_: What the schema's named primitives are on the wire.
packet_schema.json describes every packet as a tree whose leaves are named:
VAR_INT, ITEM_STACK, COMPONENT_PATCH. Those names are all a Go generator needs,
because the Go library has a type for each. A generator for another language has
nothing, so this file says what each name means, and gen/cmd/prims checks that
every primitive a version uses is defined here.
A definition is one of three shapes:
a node tree, in the same vocabulary the schema itself uses;
{k: bits}, when the value is bit fields inside one integer, offset counted from
{k: native}, when no composition describes it and every language implements it
A definition may name another primitive; a reader resolves that recursively.
Each entry records the Java member it was read from. They were derived from the
bytecode of the 26.2 server jar and checked a second time against it; javap them
with `go run ./gen/cmd/javap` before changing anything here.

BIT_SET.note: Byte-for-byte a LONG_ARRAY (var-int word count, then that many big-endian longs), interpreted as java.util.BitSet.valueOf(long[]): bit i is bit (i mod 64) of word i/64 counting from the least significant bit, and the writer trims the word count to the last word that has a bit set.

BLOCK_POS.java: net/minecraft/network/FriendlyByteBuf.readBlockPos(ByteBuf) -> net/minecraft/core/BlockPos.of(J); layout from BlockPos.<clinit> + getX/getY/getZ(J) + asLong(III)
BLOCK_POS.note: One big-endian signed 64-bit long packing three two's-complement fields: x in bits 38-63, z in bits 12-37, y in bits 0-11.

def.note: one byte; 0 is false, any non-zero byte is true; the writer emits 1 for true

BOOL.java: net/minecraft/network/codec/ByteBufCodecs$1.decode (the object put into ByteBufCodecs.BOOL) and net/minecraft/network/FriendlyByteBuf.readBoolean, both io/netty/buffer/AbstractByteBuf.readBoolean
BOOL.note: A single byte: 0 means false and any non-zero byte means true, and true is written as 1.

BYTE.note: One byte read as a signed two's-complement value in -128..127.

BYTE_ARRAY.note: A var-int count then exactly that many raw bytes; a node's `max` only caps the count and is not on the wire - note Mojang checks only count > max, not count < 0, so a generated reader must reject a negative count itself.

CHUNK_POS.java: net/minecraft/network/FriendlyByteBuf.readChunkPos -> net/minecraft/world/level/ChunkPos.unpack(J); ChunkPos.pack(II) and the ChunkPos(int,int) record constructor
CHUNK_POS.note: One big-endian signed 64-bit long with x in the low 32 bits and z in the high 32 bits - so on the wire the four bytes of z arrive FIRST, then the four bytes of x.

COMPONENT_PATCH.note: Two var-int counts first, then addedCount components (each a TYPED_DATA_COMPONENT) and then removedCount component-type ids — it is NOT two `list`s, because both counts precede both runs.

CONTAINER_ID.note: A plain var-int with no bias or offset - the token only records that the number identifies an open container.

DELIMITED_COMPONENT_PATCH.note: COMPONENT_PATCH with every added value preceded by its length in bytes, so a reader can step over a component it does not know.

DOUBLE.note: Eight big-endian bytes reinterpreted as an IEEE-754 double-precision float.

ENTITY_DATA.note: Entries of { unsigned-byte field index, var-int serializer id, value in that serializer's codec } repeated UNTIL an index byte of 0xff, which is the terminator and carries nothing after it; the `while` clause is the schema's end-of-list condition, not a continue condition. The serializer ids and their value types are the serializers list of entity_data.json.

def.note: No length prefix at all: read exactly ceil(bits/8) raw bytes, where `bits` is the node's own parameter (the schema emits it as a sibling of `t`). Bit i is bit (i mod 8) of byte i/8, counting from the least significant bit of each byte. In 26.2 the only size used is bits=20, i.e. exactly 3 bytes.

FIXED_BIT_SET.note: A bit set whose size the packet already knows: ceil(bits/8) bare bytes with no count, LSB-first within each byte.

def.note: exactly `len` raw bytes, no count on the wire; `len` is the constant on the node

FIXED_BYTES.note: A block of exactly `len` bytes with no length prefix; all six occurrences in the 26.2 schema are len 256, the chat message-signature block, and several are conditional fields (present only when the preceding packed id says so).

FLOAT.note: Four big-endian bytes reinterpreted as an IEEE-754 single-precision float.

GAME_PROFILE_PROPERTIES.java: net/minecraft/network/codec/ByteBufCodecs$32.decode/encode (the class ByteBufCodecs.<clinit> pc 255 stores in GAME_PROFILE_PROPERTIES)
GAME_PROFILE_PROPERTIES.note: A var-int count of at most 16 properties, each a name string (max 64 chars), a value string (max 32767 chars) and a boolean-prefixed optional signature string (max 1024 chars); every string is a var-int BYTE length then UTF-8, and each max is a character cap.

IDENTIFIER.note: Exactly a STRING (var-int byte length + UTF-8), cap 32767 characters, whose text is a namespaced id "namespace:path"; a string with no ':' (or a leading ':') takes the default "minecraft" namespace.

INSTANT.note: An ordinary big-endian signed 64-bit long holding milliseconds since the Unix epoch (Instant.ofEpochMilli).

def.note: four bytes, big-endian, signed two's complement

INT.note: Four bytes, most significant first, read as a signed two's-complement 32-bit value.

ITEM_STACK.note: Byte-for-byte OPTIONAL_ITEM_STACK with the empty encoding forbidden: the count is always at least one, so the item id and the component patch always follow. The creative mode slot packet sends UNTRUSTED_ITEM_STACK instead, which delimits its components.

JSON_TEXT.note: A label on an ordinary STRING read - var-int byte length + UTF-8 bytes - whose text is then parsed as JSON; `max` on the node is the character cap given to lenientJson (262144 for login disconnect, 32767 for the status response).

def.note: eight bytes, big-endian, signed two's complement

LONG.note: Eight bytes, most significant first, read as a signed two's-complement 64-bit value.

LONG_ARRAY.note: A var-int count followed by that many big-endian signed 64-bit longs; the decoder rejects a count larger than readableBytes()/8.

def.note: Read one unsigned byte b0. If b0 == 0 the value is (0,0,0) and NOTHING further is read. Otherwise read one unsigned byte b1 and a big-endian unsigned 32-bit integer u, and form the 48-bit value v = (u << 16) | (b1 << 8) | b0 (note this is mixed-endian on the wire: wire bytes are v[7:0], v[15:8], then u big-endian, i.e. v[47:40], v[39:32], v[31:24], v[23:16]). scale = b0 & 3; if (b0 & 4) != 0 then read a VarInt h and set scale |= ((h as unsigned 32-bit) << 2). Then x = q(v >> 3) * scale, y = q(v >> 18) * scale, z = q(v >> 33) * scale, where q(w) = min(w & 0x7FFF, 32766) * 2 / 32766 - 1. The components therefore occupy bits 3-17, 18-32 and 33-47 of v.

LP_VEC3.java: net/minecraft/network/LpVec3.read(ByteBuf) and LpVec3.unpack(J); reached from net/minecraft/world/phys/Vec3.LP_STREAM_CODEC = StreamCodec.of(LpVec3::write, LpVec3::read)
LP_VEC3.note: Minecraft's low-precision packed vector: a 1-byte zero marker, else 6 mixed-endian bytes holding three 15-bit quantised components plus 3 scale/flag bits, optionally followed by a VarInt carrying the rest of the scale.

MESSAGE_SIGNATURE.note: A 256-byte signature block with no length prefix; the 26.2 extractor never emits this token - the codec field it is keyed on does not exist, and signatures reach the schema as FIXED_BYTES len 256 through the inlined reader.

def.note: one tag in network form: a 1-byte tag id, then that tag's payload with no name; id 0 (TAG_End) is the whole value and carries no payload

NBT.note: One NBT tag in network form: a 1-byte tag id followed by that tag's payload with NO root name; id 0 (TAG_End) is the entire value, and whether that means "absent" or is a decode error depends on the reader (FriendlyByteBuf.readNbt returns null; ByteBufCodecs.TAG/COMPOUND_TAG throw).

OPTIONAL_ITEM_STACK.note: A var-int count; when it is <= 0 the stack is empty and nothing else is read, otherwise a var-int item registry id and a COMPONENT_PATCH follow.

OPTIONAL_ITEM_STACK_LIST.note: An ordinary var-int-counted list whose elements are OPTIONAL_ITEM_STACK, so empty stacks may appear inside it; no wire-relevant maximum.

OPTIONAL_NBT.java: net/minecraft/network/codec/ByteBufCodecs$19.decode/encode (the class ByteBufCodecs.<clinit> pc 215 stores in OPTIONAL_COMPOUND_TAG)
OPTIONAL_NBT.note: Byte-for-byte an NBT and NOT boolean-prefixed: absence is the single TAG_End byte 0x00 that NBT already allows, and when a tag is present it must be a TAG_Compound (anything else is a decode error).

OPTIONAL_TEXT.note: A boolean; when true one TEXT (a network NBT tag) follows, when false nothing follows — genuinely boolean-prefixed, unlike OPTIONAL_NBT.

def.note: One var-int: 0 means absent; any other value n means present with the value n - 1. The writer emits (value + 1) when present and 0 when absent. This is NOT the schema's `optional` node, which is a boolean followed by the value.

OPTIONAL_VAR_INT.note: A single var-int where 0 encodes absence and n > 0 encodes the value n - 1. WARNING: the extractor also attaches this token to EntityDataSerializers$2, where it is wrong - see evidence.

PUBLIC_KEY.note: A var-int length (the reader rejects above 512) then that many bytes, holding the DER X.509 SubjectPublicKeyInfo encoding of an RSA public key; the writer imposes no cap of its own.

REGISTRY_KEY.note: One IDENTIFIER naming the registry itself (e.g. "minecraft:block"); the ResourceKey's root-registry parent is a static field in Java and never travels.

def.note: every byte remaining in the packet frame; no count precedes it, the length comes from the frame

REST_BYTES.note: The raw remainder of the buffer after the fields before it, with no length prefix; it is opaque bytes - when a channel is one the server knows (minecraft:brand carries a STRING) that structure is inside the blob, not described by this token.

ROTATION_BYTE.note: One signed byte covering a whole turn in 256 steps: the angle in degrees is b * 360 / 256 (b is signed, so -128..127 covers -180..+179.3).

def.note: two bytes, big-endian, signed two's complement, -32768..32767

SHORT.note: Two bytes, most significant first, read as a signed two's-complement 16-bit value.

def.note: a var-int byte count, then exactly that many UTF-8 bytes

STRING.note: Var-int BYTE count followed by that many UTF-8 bytes; where a cap applies it is a CHARACTER count (the byte length is rejected above 3x the cap before reading, the decoded String.length() above the cap after), and in the 26.2 schema no prim STRING node carries a cap at all - the separate `string` node kind is what carries `max`.

TEXT.note: A chat component carried as exactly one network NBT tag (parsed with NbtOps): a TAG_String for a plain literal, a non-empty TAG_List of components, or a TAG_Compound — TAG_End is rejected, and there is no length prefix on the codec field itself.

TYPED_DATA_COMPONENT.note: A var-int data_component_type registry id, then the value in that component type's own stream codec, with no length prefix. The cases are the components section of packet_schema.json, keyed by the same registry name, which casesFrom points at. It is marked recursive because several components (container, bundle_contents, charged_projectiles, use_remainder, sulfur_cube_content) hold item stacks, which hold a component patch again: the format recurses, so a reader has to stop inlining here and recurse at run time instead.

def.note: one byte, unsigned, 0..255 (the same byte as BYTE, interpreted without sign)

UNSIGNED_BYTE.note: The same single byte as BYTE, but interpreted as unsigned 0..255.

UNSIGNED_SHORT.note: The same two big-endian bytes as SHORT, interpreted as unsigned 0..65535; the writer truncates the int to 16 bits.

UNTRUSTED_ITEM_STACK.note: OPTIONAL_ITEM_STACK with the delimited component patch: a count of at most zero is an empty stack and nothing follows it.

UUID.note: Sixteen bytes: the high 64 bits then the low 64 bits, each a big-endian signed long - the same as writing the 128-bit value big-endian.

def.note: unsigned LEB128 of the 32-bit two's-complement pattern: seven data bits per byte, least significant group first, high bit set means another byte follows; at most 5 bytes

VAR_INT.java: net/minecraft/network/VarInt.read (reached from net/minecraft/network/codec/ByteBufCodecs$6.decode for ByteBufCodecs.VAR_INT and from net/minecraft/network/FriendlyByteBuf.readVarInt)
VAR_INT.note: Little-endian base-128: each byte carries seven data bits, the high bit says another byte follows, and a value is at most five bytes; negative numbers are the 32-bit two's-complement pattern, so they always take five bytes.

VAR_INT_ARRAY.note: A var-int count followed by that many var-ints; the no-arg overload caps the count at readableBytes().

VAR_INT_LIST.note: Identical on the wire to VAR_INT_ARRAY - a var-int count then that many var-ints - differing only in the Java container (IntList rather than int[]).

def.note: unsigned LEB128 of the 64-bit two's-complement pattern: seven data bits per byte, least significant group first, high bit set means another byte follows; at most 10 bytes

VAR_LONG.java: net/minecraft/network/VarLong.read (reached from net/minecraft/network/codec/ByteBufCodecs$8.decode for ByteBufCodecs.VAR_LONG and from net/minecraft/network/FriendlyByteBuf.readVarLong)
VAR_LONG.note: The same base-128 scheme as VAR_INT but over 64 bits and at most ten bytes; negative numbers are the 64-bit two's-complement pattern and always take ten bytes.
